newsitem.title: USA: Colorado tax measure may hit nonprofit debt - S&P.
newsitem.headline: Colorado tax measure may hit nonprofit debt - S&P.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp warned on Monday that a Colorado ballot measure could undermine the credit ratings of several nonprofit entities in the state.
Colorado voters on November 5 will decide whether property tax exemptions for various nonprofit entities should be continued.

If the ballot measure, Amendment 11, is passed, S&P said the ratings on seven health care providers and one research center could be lowered. If other states take similar steps, the ratings in all nonprofit areas may be at risk for downgrades, S&P said in its CreditWeek Municipal publication.
S&P said the BBB-minus rating on the National Jewish Center for Immunology, already under pressure and under review with negative implications, may be particularly hard it.

The National Center for Atmospheric Research, which has fared reasonably well in an environment where the outlook for research in general is a concern, may face a tax liability of $550,000 annually, S&P said.

The rating agency said lower rated credits, particularly in the BBB category, are most likely to suffer rating downgrades since these credits are weaker to start with, and the capacity to absorb increased costs is minimal.

S&P said many other states and local governments are grappling with the issue of tax exemption. California, Texas, New York, Pennsylvania, Oregon, the District of Columbia and Montana, among others, have at one time or another raised the question of tax exemption eligibility, S&P said.
"Regardless of the outcome of this specific vote (in Colorado), it is clear that charitable status, and all its benefits, will remain an issue for years to come," S&P said.
